title: Rubber Duck pH Titration Lab
description: A virtual chemistry lab where the user performs an acid-base titration using a WaterBottle as the burette and a Duck floating in a beaker as the pH indicator. The user must carefully dispense reagent from the bottle into the beaker, observe color changes in the solution, monitor the pH curve on a live graph, and identify the equivalence point within an acceptable tolerance.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load Duck.glb and WaterBottle.glb. Scene setup: Place a transparent glass beaker (cylinder geometry with MeshPhysicalMaterial, transmission=0.8) at center. Position the Duck model floating inside the beaker, bobbing gently with a sine-wave animation. Place the WaterBottle model above and to the right of the beaker, tilted at 30 degrees, acting as a burette. Fill the beaker with a colored liquid plane that changes color based on pH (red at pH 1, orange at 4, yellow at 6, green at 7, blue at 9, purple at 14). Add a 2D HTML overlay panel showing a live pH vs volume graph drawn on a canvas element. Camera: perspective at position (0, 3, 5) looking at origin. Lighting: ambient light 0.4 intensity plus one directional light casting soft shadows. Interactions (7 steps with validation): Step 1: User clicks a 'Select Acid' button choosing HCl concentration from a dropdown (0.1M, 0.5M, 1.0M). Step 2: User clicks 'Fill Beaker' to set initial acid volume (validate 10-50 mL via slider). Step 3: User clicks the WaterBottle to activate dispensing mode; the bottle tilts further and a particle stream (small sphere geometries) flows into the beaker. Step 4: User controls NaOH dispensing rate with a slider (0.5-5.0 mL/s); validate range. Step 5: User clicks 'Dispense' repeatedly; each click adds a measured volume. The liquid color transitions smoothly, the Duck bobs more vigorously near equivalence point, and the pH graph updates in real time. Step 6: User must click 'Stop' within ±0.5 mL of the calculated equivalence point. Validate the total dispensed volume against the stoichiometric equivalence. Step 7: Display results panel showing accuracy percentage, final pH, and whether the titration was successful (equivalence point hit within tolerance). Add a reset button to restart. The Duck should quack (console log) when pH crosses 7. All parameter inputs must be validated with visual error feedback on out-of-range values.
